---
title: "How do I calculate a weighted expected value from discrete outcomes?"
---

## Question

How do I calculate a weighted expected value from discrete outcomes?

## Work through it

Identify every possible numeric outcome and its probability; verify nonnegative probabilities summing to one; multiply each outcome by its probability and add.

## Worked example: mtcars

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("mtcars")
counts <- table(d$cyl)
outcomes <- as.numeric(names(counts))
weights <- as.numeric(prop.table(counts))
answer <- ru_apply("discrete_expectation", x=outcomes, y=weights)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(answer["expected"]),mean(d$cyl))))
```

The expected cylinder count under this *empirical distribution* equals the mean cylinder count in the recorded cars. An expected value need not be one of the possible individual outcomes.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("discrete_expectation", x=your_numeric_outcomes, y=your_probabilities)
```

If outcome probabilities are unknown, you cannot calculate a theoretical expectation without a defensible way to estimate them.

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("discrete_expectation")` before treating a calculation as an inference.
